With enclosing box $C$, $GIoU=IoU-|C\setminus(A\cup B)|/|C|$, so $1-GIoU$ adds an enclosure penalty even when overlap is zero. DIoU adds normalized squared center distance: $L_{DIoU}=1-IoU+\rho^2(b,b^*)/c^2$, where $c$ is the enclosing-box diagonal. CIoU additionally penalizes aspect-ratio disagreement. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.09630) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.08287)

Specifically, $v=\frac4{\pi^2}(\arctan(w^*/h^*)-\arctan(w/h))^2$ and the usual weighting is $\alpha=v/(1-IoU+v)$, giving $L_{CIoU}=L_{DIoU}+\alpha v$. Standard IoU is locally flat when boxes remain disjoint, so it lacks a useful overlap gradient there. These extensions add geometric signals but still have degenerate/nonsmooth cases.
